title: The "All-or-Nothing" Config Rollout
damaged_code:
```bash
# Push configuration update to 100% of hosts concurrently
for host in $(get_all_servers); do
    copy_config_and_restart $host
done
```
pattern: Applying configuration changes or profile updates to all production hosts or services simultaneously.
why_bad: Ensures that a single configuration bug or typo triggers immediate, 100% system downtime. It leaves no safety margin to detect errors and roll back before users are impacted.
detection: Deploy tools or script patterns that lack staging parameters, canary gates, or gradual traffic progression features.
counterexample:
```bash
# Push to canary node first; verify health before proceeding
deploy_config_to_subset "canary"
verify_health_status "canary" || abort_rollout
```
fix: Design configuration distribution pipelines around canary groups; apply changes to a tiny percentage of machines first, verifying health before completing the rollout.
source: Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright - *Software Engineering at Google_ Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 23 / Chapter 24; Heather Adkins et al., - *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 5.
